b2-pluralismo-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The 1989 Convention
b2-pluralismo-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading an article about indigenous rights, and he asks if the problems are solved.
b2-pluralismo-01.prompt: Tell Carlos that the convention exists but problems remain.
cues: Say when the convention dates from
b2-pluralismo-01.target: El Convenio 169 es de 1989; no obstante, muchos conflictos por la consulta siguen abiertos.
b2-pluralismo-01.english: Convention 169 dates from 1989; nevertheless, many conflicts over consultation remain open.
b2-pluralismo-01.canDo: I can contrast two facts with *sin embargo* and *no obstante*.

b2-pluralismo-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Peasant Patrols
b2-pluralismo-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are watching a documentary about the rondas campesinas, and she asks about the law.
b2-pluralismo-02.prompt: Tell Meg about the law that recognised the patrols.
b2-pluralismo-02.target: La ley de 2003 es la norma con la que Perú reconoció a las rondas campesinas.
b2-pluralismo-02.english: The 2003 law is the rule with which Peru recognised the peasant patrols.
b2-pluralismo-02.canDo: I can describe a place, a law or an institution with *en la que*, *con la que* and other relatives with a preposition.

b2-pluralismo-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Rivers With Rights
b2-pluralismo-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading about the Atrato river, and he asks what you think about legal protection for rivers.
b2-pluralismo-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what you think is important for rivers.
b2-pluralismo-03.target: Es importante que los ríos tengan protección legal.
b2-pluralismo-03.english: It is important that rivers have legal protection.
b2-pluralismo-03.canDo: I can say what should happen to rivers and forests, with *es importante que* and *es necesario que* + subjunctive.

b2-pluralismo-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Language Becomes Official
b2-pluralismo-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are listening to a talk about languages, and she asks about Paraguay.
b2-pluralismo-04.prompt: Tell Meg why Guaraní is an official language of Paraguay.
cues: Say that Guaraní is official next to Spanish
b2-pluralismo-04.target: A raíz de la Constitución de 1992, el guaraní es lengua oficial de Paraguay junto al castellano.
b2-pluralismo-04.english: As a result of the 1992 Constitution, Guaraní is an official language of Paraguay together with Spanish.
b2-pluralismo-04.canDo: I can give a cause with *debido a* and *a raíz de*.

b2-pluralismo-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Escazú Agreement
b2-pluralismo-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading an article about defenders of the environment, and he asks what the Escazú Agreement says.
b2-pluralismo-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what the Escazú Agreement says States must do.
cues: Say whom the States must protect
b2-pluralismo-05.target: Según el Acuerdo de Escazú, los Estados han de proteger a las personas defensoras del ambiente.
b2-pluralismo-05.english: According to the Escazú Agreement, States must protect people who defend the environment.
b2-pluralismo-05.canDo: I can say what must be done, in a formal register, with *han de*, *has de* and other *haber de* + infinitive forms.

b2-pluralismo-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Languages and Migration
b2-pluralismo-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing a short talk about native languages, and she asks for one cause and one remedy.
b2-pluralismo-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg why children are losing their languages and what exists to help.
b2-pluralismo-consolidation.target: Debido a la migración a las ciudades, muchos niños ya no aprenden la lengua de sus abuelos; no obstante, existen aplicaciones para aprenderla.
b2-pluralismo-consolidation.english: Because of migration to the cities, many children no longer learn their grandparents' language; nevertheless, there are apps to learn it.
b2-pluralismo-consolidation.canDo: I can use contrast and cause connectors, relatives, value judgments and *haber de* to talk about indigenous rights.
